title.vi: Cửa hàng trực tuyến đáng ngờ

summary.en: A new online store is selling laptops at 64% off. Before the Technology Club transfers more than 100 million VND, find out whether the store can be trusted.
summary.vi: Một cửa hàng trực tuyến mới đang bán laptop giảm giá 64%. Trước khi Câu lạc bộ Công nghệ chuyển hơn 100 triệu đồng, hãy xác minh xem cửa hàng này có đáng tin hay không.

topic: E-commerce, online advertising and source reliability

briefing.en: The Riverside University Technology Club wants to place a group order for twelve Zentrix ProBook 14 laptops and twenty pairs of headphones from TechNova Deals, a new online store that has been advertising huge discounts on social media. Before the club treasurer, Mai Pham, transfers more than 100 million VND, the club's faculty adviser has asked the English Detective Agency to find out whether the store can be trusted. One club member, Khoa Nguyen, has already bought headphones from the store and is still waiting for them. Evaluate every source carefully, separate verified facts from marketing claims, interview the people involved and write a report with a cautious, evidence-based conclusion and practical recommendations.
briefing.vi: Câu lạc bộ Công nghệ của Đại học Riverside muốn đặt mua chung mười hai laptop Zentrix ProBook 14 và hai mươi chiếc tai nghe từ TechNova Deals, một cửa hàng trực tuyến mới đang quảng cáo giảm giá rất mạnh trên mạng xã hội. Trước khi thủ quỹ Mai Pham chuyển khoản hơn 100 triệu đồng, cố vấn của câu lạc bộ đã nhờ English Detective Agency kiểm tra xem cửa hàng này có đáng tin cậy không. Một thành viên, Khoa Nguyen, đã mua tai nghe của cửa hàng và đến nay vẫn chưa nhận được hàng. Hãy đánh giá cẩn thận từng nguồn thông tin, tách biệt sự thật đã được xác minh với lời quảng cáo, phỏng vấn những người liên quan và viết báo cáo với kết luận thận trọng, dựa trên bằng chứng cùng các khuyến nghị thiết thực.

objectives.en: Evaluate the reliability of each source: the store's own pages, the advertisement, the Council's alert and the independent checks.
objectives.vi: Đánh giá độ tin cậy của từng nguồn: các trang của chính cửa hàng, quảng cáo, thông báo của Hội đồng và các kết quả kiểm tra độc lập.

objectives.en: Separate verifiable evidence from marketing claims that cannot be confirmed.
objectives.vi: Phân biệt bằng chứng có thể kiểm chứng với những lời quảng cáo không thể xác nhận.

objectives.en: Interview Khoa, the consumer-protection officer and the e-commerce expert.
objectives.vi: Phỏng vấn Khoa, cán bộ bảo vệ người tiêu dùng và chuyên gia thương mại điện tử.

objectives.en: Write a report with a cautious, evidence-based conclusion and practical recommendations.
objectives.vi: Viết báo cáo với kết luận thận trọng, dựa trên bằng chứng và các khuyến nghị thiết thực.

documents.title: Consumer Alert No. 05/2027: Online Shopping Warning List
documents.body:
SOUTHERN CONSUMER PROTECTION COUNCIL – CONSUMER ALERT No. 05/2027

The Council has seen a sharp rise in complaints about new online stores that advertise electronics on social media at very low prices. Before you buy, please check the points below.

What a legitimate online seller must provide: Every business that sells goods online must clearly display a business registration number, a physical address and its return conditions on its website. If any of these is missing, consumers should not pay in advance.

Common warning signs:
- prices far below the normal market price, often with a countdown timer;
- payment accepted only by bank transfer, especially to a personal account;
- many similar five-star reviews posted within a short time;
- a website that was created only a few weeks or months ago;
- a seller that cannot be found in the National Business Registry.

Websites currently on the warning list (complaints received as of 19 May 2027):

| Website | Complaints | Status |
|---|---|---|
| gadgetzone-sale.net | 31 | Referred to police |
| technova-deals.shop | 14 | Under investigation |
| mega-phone-outlet.com | 6 | Under investigation |

Being on this list does not mean that a seller has been found guilty. It means that the Council has received complaints and is checking them.

To report a website, call the consumer hotline 1800 0000 or visit the Council office in District 1.

documents.title: Domain and Business Registration Lookup – technova-deals.shop

meta.Prepared by: Dr. Quang Do, Faculty of Commerce, Riverside University

documents.body:
1. Domain record
The domain technova-deals.shop was registered on 18 April 2027, about two weeks before the advertisement appeared. The owner's identity is hidden by a paid privacy service, and the website is hosted on a server outside Vietnam.

2. National Business Registry
A search of the National Business Registry for 'TechNova Deals', 'TechNova' and the website address found no registered business with these names. No business registration number is linked to the website.

3. Customer reviews
We compared 40 reviews on the store's website with reviews on other shopping sites. 27 of them use exactly the same wording as reviews posted for different products on three other websites between 2025 and 2026, so they were most likely copied.

4. Product images
The product photos are identical to the official images published by the manufacturer, Zentrix. This is common practice and does not show whether a seller is genuine.

5. Brand authorisation
Zentrix Vietnam's public list of authorised resellers, checked on 21 May 2027, does not include TechNova Deals. We have asked Zentrix to confirm this in writing, but no reply has been received yet.

Summary: the store cannot be linked to any registered business, and several of its trust signals appear to be false. The Council should continue its investigation before making a final decision.

characters.name: Khoa Nguyen
characters.role: Third-year IT student and club member who bought headphones from the store

facts.text: Khoa transferred 390,000 VND on the evening of 3 May 2027 for one pair of SoundMax Air headphones, and three weeks later he still has not received them.
Since 15 May nobody has answered Khoa on the store's live chat, and the hotline number has been switched off every time he called.
Khoa found TechNova Deals through the sponsored ChatterBox advert that a friend shared, and he did not check whether the store was registered before paying.
Khoa wanted to pay cash on delivery, but the store told him that sale items could only be paid for by bank transfer.

characters.name: Ms. Vo Thu Ha
characters.role: Complaints officer, Southern Consumer Protection Council
characters.personality: Calm, professional and careful with words; never says more than the Council can officially confirm.
characters.background: Ms. Ha handles online shopping complaints at the Council and helped prepare Consumer Alert No. 05/2027. She asked Dr. Do to carry out technical checks on several websites.
characters.greeting: Good afternoon. I'm Vo Thu Ha from the Southern Consumer Protection Council. I can share what the Council has officially recorded.

facts.text: By 19 May 2027 the Council had received 14 complaints about technova-deals.shop, all from buyers who paid by bank transfer and received nothing.
The Council's check on technova-deals.shop is still open, and no official decision about the store has been made yet.
Under consumer rules, an online seller has to show its business registration number, a physical address and its return conditions on its website.
People who have already paid should keep their receipts and screenshots, contact their bank quickly and file a complaint with the Council.

characters.background: Dr. Do teaches e-commerce and online consumer behaviour. He sometimes helps the Consumer Protection Council by carrying out technical checks on suspicious websites.
characters.greeting: Hello, I'm Quang Do. I look at websites the way a detective looks at fingerprints. What do you need to know?

facts.text: On 21 May 2027 Dr. Do carried out a domain and business-registry lookup on technova-deals.shop for the Council and wrote a short report on the results.
For a new laptop model, a discount of more than 60% is far below normal market prices; genuine clearance sales of new models are usually much smaller.
Fake online shops often copy reviews from other websites or post many similar five-star reviews in a short time to look popular.
Official product photos can be copied by anyone from the manufacturer's website, so they say nothing about who the seller is.

restricted.topic: Personal data of the domain owner

conclusion.question: Based on the evidence, what is the most reasonable conclusion about TechNova Deals?

options.text: The store is unreliable and very likely fraudulent: no registered business exists, its reviews are copied, its prices are unrealistic and it gives no return address. The club should not pay, although the Council has not made a final decision yet.
The store is a genuine business that is overloaded by high demand; Khoa's order is only delayed, so the club can safely place its order.
The Council has officially proven that the store is a criminal scam run by Tran Van Binh, who has stolen money from all 2,814 reviewers.
The store is trustworthy because it has thousands of five-star reviews, a famous reviewer's recommendation and official distributor status.

unsupportedClaims: The Council has officially confirmed that TechNova Deals is a criminal scam (it is still under investigation).
Tran Van Binh is the owner of the store (the receipt only shows that he holds the bank account).
Linh Tech Talk was paid to take part in the scam (there is no evidence about the reviewer at all).
All 2,814 reviewers lost their money (the reviews themselves appear to be copied or fake).
Zentrix has officially confirmed that the store is not its distributor (Zentrix has not replied yet).

writingTask.prompt: Write an investigation report for Ms. Diep Tran, the Technology Club's faculty adviser, on whether the club should place its group order with TechNova Deals. Summarise the case, evaluate how reliable the main sources are, present the verified evidence, point out which claims are still unverified, state a cautious conclusion and give recommendations for the club and for Khoa.
writingTask.audience: Ms. Diep Tran, faculty adviser of the Riverside University Technology Club
keyPoints: Concludes that the store is unreliable / very likely fraudulent and that the club should not pay.
Uses independent evidence: no registered business found and no registration number displayed.
Mentions copied or near-identical reviews and/or the review dated before the domain existed.
Notes the unrealistic price, the missing return address and the payment to a personal account.
Distinguishes unverified claims (influencer, 4.9 rating, official distributor, since 2019) from verified facts.
Stays cautious: the Council has received complaints but has not made a final decision.
Recommends practical steps for Khoa (receipt, bank, complaint) and for the club.

documents: Start with the store's own pages, then compare them with independent sources such as the Council's alert.
For each document, ask who wrote it and whether that person or company benefits if you believe it.
Look closely at dates: when was the website created, and when were the reviews posted?
evidence: Highlight claims about the store's history, registration, reviews, payment and returns.
Laptop specifications and the number of likes are true, but they do not tell you whether the store is honest.
Pair each claim made by the store with an independent fact that confirms or contradicts it.
interviews: Ask Khoa how he paid and whether the store still answers him.
Ask Ms. Ha about complaints and whether the Council has made a final decision.
Ask Dr. Do whether anyone has checked the domain and the business registry.
analysis: Information that comes only from the store itself is unverified unless an independent source confirms it.
Choose a conclusion that is as strong as the evidence – but no stronger.
Being on a warning list is not the same as being found guilty, so keep your conclusion cautious.
report: Use the five sections: summary, source evaluation, evidence, conclusion, recommendations.
Use hedging language such as 'very likely', 'appears to' and 'there is no evidence that'.
Give separate recommendations for the club, for Khoa and for other students.

sampleSolution.report:
Summary: The Technology Club planned to spend about 115 million VND on laptops and headphones from TechNova Deals, a new online store advertised on social media. Khoa Nguyen paid 390,000 VND on 3 May 2027 and has still not received his order.

Source evaluation: Most of the positive information comes from the store itself, so it is not reliable. In contrast, the Council's alert, Dr. Do's registry lookup and Khoa's bank receipt are independent and can be verified.

Evidence: The laptop is sold at 64% below its original price, which is unrealistic for a new model. The website shows no business registration number and no return address, although the Council says every online seller must display both. Moreover, the registry search found no registered business with the store's name, and the domain was only registered on 18 April 2027. In addition, 27 reviews were copied from other websites, and Khoa's money went to a personal account. The Council has received 14 complaints. However, the influencer recommendation, the 4.9 rating and the claim of 50,000 customers since 2019 remain unverified.

Conclusion: The store appears to be unreliable and is very likely fraudulent, although the Council has not made a final decision yet.

Recommendations: The club should not transfer any money. Khoa should keep his receipt, contact his bank immediately and file a complaint with the Council. Finally, members should always check a seller's registration before paying online.
